context: Interactive tech demo and data visualization — a 3-level org chart that morphs between sunburst and icicle layouts via D3 arc-to-rect interpolation
first_impression: Clean and colorful sunburst with a deliberate palette, but the chart overflows the viewport and clips the bottom third of the visualization.
what_works: The Tol bright palette with per-depth desaturation is a genuine design choice over default Category10, giving the rings a coherent tonal relationship. Typography has real hierarchy: bold title, muted subtitle, weighted inner-ring labels vs. lighter team labels.
what_doesnt: The chart is clipped at the bottom of the viewport — the Design, UX Research, and bottom Marketing segments are cut off, which is a concrete layout bug undermining the 'does it work at rendered size' check. The overall composition feels utilitarian rather than considered: the button sits awkwardly above the chart with no visual integration, and the 1200×800 SVG with zero margins leaves no breathing room between the chart edge and viewport boundary.
